rationale: This record is a brief newspaper dispatch reporting on a 12-acre industrial hemp farm losing irrigation access from a federally controlled water source in Montana. It clearly fails Criterion 1 (agricultural irrigation rather than household or community water or sanitation service access; E07), Criterion 3 (news article rather than an empirical research study or systematic review), and Criterion 4 (crop loss rather than domestic water or sanitation access).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Excluded under both narrow and plain readings of Criterion 2 because the record concerns agricultural irrigation water for a commercial industrial hemp crop (E07) and is a short news report rather than an empirical study or systematic review.

evidence_quotes.quote: Helena Valley hemp crop dries up amid stagnant legal dispute
A 12-acre crop of hemp plants in the Helena Valley died after getting caught up in a legal dispute over water access this summer.
Aug. 08--It turns out seedlings dry out in the Montana sun quicker than the federal government can act.
